results.title: Define DPMO
results.content: # Define: Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO). Sigma levels determine the rate of defects and are a standardized measure of the error rate of a process, based on the Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) estimate. As the name suggests, Defects per million opportunities (DPMO) is the number of defects in a process per one million opportunities. Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) is a statistical metric used to quantify the number of defects in a process per one million opportunities for defects to occur. ## The Power of Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) in Six Sigma Projects. ## Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) used in each stage of DMAIC. Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) is a key metric used in Six Sigma methodology to quantify the performance of a process and track improvements. Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) is a fundamental concept in Six Sigma, serving as a beacon of quality and process improvement across various industries.

Defects Per Million Opportunities: The universal language of quality that allows us to compare the complexity of a microchip with the simplicity of a paperclip. DPMO levels the playing field by counting the *opportunities* for error, not just the errors. How does your DPMO score translate to the "Sigma Level"? As you reduce opportunities for error (improve processes), your DPMO drops drastically, and your Sigma level climbs. This is why 6σ is 3.4 DPMO, not 0.002 DPMO. results.title: Defects per million opportunities (DPMO) | Quality Gurus
results.content: In Six Sigma, Defects per Million Opportunities (DPMO) is the measure of the process performance. A defect is the non-conformance on one of many possible quality characteristics of a unit that causes customer dissatisfaction. A unit which has one or more defects is a defective unit. However, the whole unit (the page) is the defective unit. The term DPMO uses the count of defects and not the defectives. ##### Defects per Unit:. Defects per Unit (DPU) is a measure of the average number of defects per unit. The number of defect opportunities in a unit (product, process or service) is related to the complexity of the unit. Defects per opportunity (DPO) is the number of defects identified in a sample divided by the total number of defect opportunities. **Examples:** In the previous example we identified 15 defect opportunities per unit. There is a relationship between the DPMO and the Sigma Level of the process.
